q: What is the correct Fock-cutoff Lindblad simulation size to faithfully reproduce the Chuang-Yamamoto QND regeneration step, and how does simulator cost scale vs. fidelity error?
basis: Our replication used the 3-qubit bit-flip code analog rather than run the paper's actual photonic dual-rail + cross-Kerr-QND protocol, because the Fock/probe/Kerr requirements were not budgeted; the true cost of doing the paper's own scheme numerically is unknown.
next_steps: Build a QuTiP Lindblad simulator with two rails at Fock cutoff N=2..4, a probe mode with cross-Kerr coupling, and a homodyne measurement operator; sweep cutoff and compare regenerated-qubit fidelity to the analytic e^{-gamma} success prediction.

q: How sensitive is the dual-rail regeneration scheme to arm-loss asymmetry epsilon = |gamma_a - gamma_abar|, i.e., what is the residual which-path leakage as a function of the imbalance the paper explicitly forbids?
basis: Our 3-qubit analog assumes perfectly symmetric per-qubit channels; the paper insists on 'balanced' loss but never quantifies the tolerance. This is likely the dominant error term in any real optical implementation.
next_steps: In the QuTiP Lindblad model of Q1, sweep gamma_abar = gamma_a * (1 + epsilon) for epsilon in [1e-4, 1e-1] and report the qubit infidelity vs. epsilon curve, plus the equivalent implicit which-path information in bits.

q: At what per-qubit gate error and stabilizer-measurement error does the 3-qubit code's quadratic advantage disappear, i.e., where is the pseudo-threshold when the syndrome extraction is itself noisy?
basis: Our reproduction assumes perfect stabilizer measurement and perfect CNOTs. This is the largest gap between our tabletop match to 3p^2 - 2p^3 and any hardware-relevant claim.
next_steps: Extend repetition_code_sim.py to insert depolarizing noise of strength epsilon_gate on each CNOT and epsilon_meas on each stabilizer readout; run a 2-D (p, epsilon) sweep with N=10^4 per point and identify the crossover surface where p_code(p, epsilon) = p.

q: What is the throughput cost (success-probability curve) of the paper's detect-and-post-select scheme relative to the 3-qubit correct-and-keep code at matched residual infidelity?
basis: The paper does not tabulate discard rate vs. residual error; our analog changes paradigm entirely (correction, never discards). A quantitative comparison is missing on both sides.
next_steps: For a fixed target logical infidelity 1-F* in {1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5}, compute (a) the gamma required by the Chuang-Yamamoto post-select scheme and its corresponding success probability e^{-gamma}, and (b) the p range where 3p^2 - 2p^3 <= 1 - F* for the repetition code; plot resource-per-good-qubit vs. F*.

q: Does concatenating the 3-qubit bit-flip code with itself for k = 2, 3 rounds recover the full fault-tolerance-threshold behaviour, and where is the k-dependent crossover p*(k)?
basis: Our single-level result at p=0.20 still leaves ~10% residual error and the paper never discusses iterated regeneration; a 9-qubit (512x512 density matrix) two-level simulation is well within budget and would directly extend the four measured points.
next_steps: Generalize the encoder/decoder to k = 2 (9 qubits) and k = 3 (27 qubits, stochastic-trajectory MC only), rerun the Monte Carlo at p in {0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.4, 0.45, 0.5}, and locate the crossover p*(k) as a function of the code level.
